name: The Cathedral of St James in Šibenik
description: Rising above the old town of Šibenik on Croatia's Dalmatian coast, this cathedral took over a century to build, from 1431 to 1535, and is made entirely of stone, with no brick or timber in its vaults or dome. Look closely at the outer walls of the apses and you'll spot a band of 71 carved faces of men, women and children, thought to be portraits of local people. Gothic and Renaissance styles blend here.
